utterance: Hi Samuel, thanks for coming in today. Can you tell me more about the tummy pain you've been having since last night?
reply: It started last night about ten o'clock, so maybe fourteen hours. At first it sort of came and went, but it's there all the time now. It's down here on the right side, low down. Maybe a seven out of ten, though I'm not one to complain.

awards.label: Whether the pain is constant or comes and goes

utterance: Can you point to exactly where it hurts the most?
reply: Right here, low down on the right side.

utterance: Have you had any vomiting or diarrhoea with this pain?
reply: I have felt sick since the early hours and threw up once this morning, but I haven't had diarrhoea. I went normally yesterday morning and nothing since.

finding: Right lower quadrant: Marked tenderness, maximal at McBurney's point, with voluntary guarding. Central (periumbilical): Mild tenderness only. Elsewhere: soft and non-tender.

utterance: Does the pain get worse when you move around or cough?
reply: Yeah, walking hurts. Every bump in the car on the way here was awful, and coughing is the worst.

awards.label: Red flag: Whether moving, walking or coughing makes it worse

finding: Right lower quadrant: Rebound tenderness present; he winces sharply. Elsewhere: no rebound tenderness.

utterance: Have you noticed any fever or feeling hot?
reply: I felt hot and a bit shivery last night.

awards.label: Red flag: Fever, sweats or chills

utterance: Have you had any similar pain before?
reply: No, never had anything like this.

awards.label: Whether he has had this pain before

reply: Will I be able to head back to work after this, or is this going to take a while?
